lastCompletedStory.title: Review round 1 fix 001: address reviewer finding

openQuestions: US-001 AC4's oracle text (`grep -q 'self-nullifying-oracle' scripts/cam/handoff.json`) still lives, unmodified, inside scripts/cam/prd.json's acceptanceCriteria. It is structurally unfixable by any implementer session: Write/Edit/MultiEdit on scripts/cam/prd.json is hard-blocked for CAM_WORKER=1 sessions by the write-guard hook (.claude/hooks/orch-agent-allowlist.sh, matcher Write|Edit|MultiEdit), confirmed by direct Edit-tool attempt during this story (denied with 'worker-protected cam control-plane state'). The oracle will therefore continue to read RED at any future Layer B re-run against branch HEAD, for the same reason the CRITICAL finding cites: handoff.json rotates every story cycle and no longer carries US-001's content once a later story's finalize step overwrites it. Whoever authors/edits acceptanceCriteria (planner or reviewer role, not the implementer) needs to retarget that single oracle string at a durable surface -- e.g. `grep -q 'self-nullifying-oracle' scripts/cam/patterns.md` (already satisfied, since the bullet lives there permanently) -- or drop the criterion, since scripts/cam/patterns.md:906 (the new bullet appended by this story) now documents both the antipattern and this exact residual gap for whoever picks it up.
nextStoryContext: US-R1-001 (CAM-376 review round 1) addressed the CRITICAL finding at prd.json:20 (US-001 AC4's evidence oracle pointing at the rotating scripts/cam/handoff.json) within the bounds available to an implementer session: it appended a new EOF bullet to scripts/cam/patterns.md (after the US-003 bullet, blank-line separated, single physical line per the file's flat-bullet convention) that (1) names the antipattern generally -- never target scripts/cam/handoff.json (or any other per-story-rotating harness state file, e.g. scripts/cam/review-artifact.txt) as an acceptance-criterion evidence oracle, since it is overwritten every story cycle -- (2) states the durable alternative (point at the edited file's own committed text for the after-state, diff against `git show main:<path>` for the before-state, exactly the technique already used by this PRD's own AC5/AC6 pinning oracles), and (3) records the residual limitation: the implementer role cannot itself retarget the AC4 oracle string because scripts/cam/prd.json is hard-blocked from Write/Edit/MultiEdit for worker-actor (CAM_WORKER=1) sessions (verified empirically: an Edit-tool attempt against prd.json during this story was denied by .claude/hooks/orch-agent-allowlist.sh with an explicit 'worker-protected cam control-plane state' reason). No code was touched (patterns.md-only diff); scripts/cam/prd.json's pre-existing working-tree diff (the review-round findings plus the two new US-R1-00x story records, present on disk before this session started and not authored by this session) was committed as-is via `git add`+`git commit` (a Bash git operation, not the guarded Write/Edit/MultiEdit tool), which is the expected mechanism by which a review-fix implementer carries forward reviewer-authored prd.json state. US-R1-002 (the sibling WARNING-severity fix in this same review round, for the vacuous-empty-array gap in test/dispatch.test.ts's strengthened assertion) is unaffected by this story's diff and has no dependency on it.
